sources.title: Six-obligation follow-up: first attacks and hard gates
sources.notes: Source-level audit and scoped integration record for tensor admission, fixed-population yield/rank, arity-three proof explanations, PKM dual certificates, Wagner bucket variance and xedni selected lifts.

sources.title: Native exact Appendix D.4 numeric admission audit
sources.notes: Arbitrary-precision mirror of the numeric recursion guards only; it deliberately does not certify predicate or aggregate cost hypotheses.

sources.title: Native source-bound finite-field unit-explanation checker
sources.notes: Independently replays one-equation nonzero-constant conflicts and one-affine-unknown propagations against the canonical IR hash.

nodes.label: Hashed-ECDL Boolean tensor contraction bound
nodes.statement: The hashed factor-base route gives the stated subexponential ECDLP bound only when the exact tensor contraction theorem, predicate-description and entry-evaluation hypotheses, aggregate construction and space bounds, relation yield, rank and complete-cost composition all hold for one parameter family.
nodes.scope: Conditional theorem chain for the pinned hashed-ECDL construction. Bounded forced-recursion controls and the numeric admission audit do not establish its asymptotic runtime or a practical attack.
nodes.formula: 2^{O(b/(log b)^(1/4))} under the complete source hypotheses
non_implications: The live usize dispatcher does not execute the asymptotic recursive branch on a 64-bit host
The exact numeric guard audit does not certify predicate or aggregate cost

nodes.label: Exact D.4 numeric recursion boundary
nodes.statement: For even subdivided source sizes, the first root size with nonzero D.4 scale u=floor(ceil(log2 s)/131072) is s=2^131071+2; at degree two the mirrored numeric guards pass with lambda=131072, u=1, a=2, L=4 and D=2^24, while no 64-bit usize host can represent s.
nodes.scope: Exact integer guard calculation and native regression tests. This is a representation/admission fact, not the tensor theorem or a runtime measurement.
assumptions: The pinned Appendix D.4 parameter formulas
Even size after public Boolean-network subdivision

formal.notes: BigUint calculation with boundary, host-width and fail-closed degree tests.

nodes.label: Typed tensor predicate-cost certificate
nodes.statement: The public opaque predicate closure has no machine-checkable certificate of polynomial description size or the uniform entry-evaluation bound required by the contraction theorem.
nodes.scope: A typed canonical predicate family must expose a description-size measure and a compositional operation bound; a Boolean assertion or development meter is not such a certificate.

nodes.label: Tensor aggregate construction and space certificate
nodes.statement: No source-level certificate currently composes local packet, child, precision and recovery allocations into the aggregate construction-time and polynomial-space bounds required by the tensor theorem.
nodes.scope: Depth-first execution and bounded local tests are useful controls but do not prove the asymptotic aggregate bound for an admitted instance family.

nodes.label: Fixed-population prime-field yield and rank evidence
nodes.statement: The prime-field corpus lacks a write-once, fixed-budget natural-target population that simultaneously retains every decomposition count, solver failure, verified relation row and incremental-rank/support observation past the first recovery point.
nodes.scope: The historical named batch is under an explicit custody hold, and stopped aggregate records cannot reconstruct zero mass, variance, multiplicity or terminal rank. A clean successor must use public fixtures and a new identity.
failure_modes: Rank computed from a different population

nodes.label: Source-bound Fp unit-equation explanation checker
nodes.statement: Against an exact canonical-IR hash and one named source equation, the native checker independently accepts only a nonzero constant conflict or a unique affine residual a*x+b with invertible a, and rejects changed conclusions, nonlinear residuals, multiple unknowns, malformed premises and changed source IR.
nodes.scope: One finite-field lemma class. It is not a Boolean clause proof, a CaDiCaL external propagator, a complete algebraic proof log or a solver-scaling result.
assumptions: Prime-field arithmetic represented by the native IR

formal.notes: Three focused tests cover propagation, conflict, mutation and nonlinear rejection.

nodes.label: Bind Fp explanations to Boolean trail literals
nodes.statement: The checked field assignments and conclusions are not yet translated into the exact Boolean selector literals that form a SAT trail premise and propagated clause.
nodes.scope: The binding must preserve canonical variable/value semantics and fail closed on ambiguous or incomplete encodings.

nodes.label: Compose finite-field and Boolean proof logs
nodes.statement: No production external propagator currently emits clauses whose field consequence is replayed by the native kernel and whose Boolean consequence is composed with a pinned solver proof log.
nodes.scope: Stronger field lemmas such as equation combinations and guarded inversions require separate checked certificate rules before use.

nodes.label: PKM closure-dual lower-bound certificate
nodes.statement: For the degree-c closure matrix A_c with its constant column distinguished, a vector ell satisfying A_c*ell=0 and ell_constant=1 is a finite certificate that 1 is not in the generated closure and hence the closure degree is greater than c.
nodes.scope: The matrix basis, coefficient field, closure rules and constant column must be canonical and independently replayable. One certificate proves one finite lower bound, not an asymptotic family or a matrix-width bound.

nodes.label: Growing PKM closure-dual certificate family
nodes.statement: No verified family of PKM closure-dual certificates is known for degrees c(t) growing with the tower parameter t.
nodes.scope: A bounded collection of finite certificates is evidence for those cells only. A useful theorem must specify the tower family and prove the dual construction for growing t.

nodes.label: PKM closure degree to matrix-width bridge
nodes.statement: A closure- or solving-degree lower bound does not by itself lower-bound every representation's column support, nonzeros, peak frontier, memory or sparse arithmetic work; PKM lacks that representation-aware bridge.
nodes.scope: The bridge must name the canonical normal-form basis and actual work model. Projected high-memory cells are secondary checks, not a proof.

nodes.label: Relative Wagner bucket variance W
nodes.statement: For bucket weights q_c, global agreement rate delta and target-bucket rates pi_c, the relative bucket second moment is W=sum_c q_c*(pi_c/delta-1)^2.
nodes.scope: This is the statistic required to distinguish a nearly uniform filter from a bucket-concentrated signal; a first moment or aggregate agreement rate cannot recover it.
assumptions: The buckets and weights form the frozen estimator partition

nodes.label: Wagner bucket-variance scaling law
nodes.statement: No admitted native scaling panel determines how W varies with the group prime p and bucket count M for the proposed elliptic-curve representation filters.
nodes.scope: The requested panel needs exact whole-group anchors, a frozen prime/M ladder, positive and matched-marginal null controls, bias checks, checkpointing and independent replay.
nodes.formula: candidate fit W=Theta(M^a*p^(-1/2)); proof-repair direction requires a<1/2 at M=p^(1/3)

nodes.label: Wagner variance to useful filter-gain bridge
nodes.statement: Even a large or nondecaying W is only a concentration signal until a theorem converts it into an enumerable, sufficiently dense, non-generic relation filter with complete setup, memory, yield and verification costs.
nodes.scope: Small W supports a proof that the proposed filtering gain is bounded; large W breaks that repair but does not itself provide an ECDLP attack.

nodes.label: Wagner-style ECDLP representation-filter gain
nodes.statement: A Wagner-style elliptic-curve filter improves relation search only if its bucket variance scales favorably and the concentrated buckets can be enumerated and verified at the required density with a non-generic interface and complete costs.
nodes.scope: Conditional route distinct from Wagner's four-sum heuristic itself. No present W measurement or filter-gain theorem establishes this route.
assumptions: Complete relation yield and memory accounting

nodes.label: Explicit terminating xedni lift selector
nodes.statement: No explicit xedni selector is proved to terminate uniformly on every finite-field input in a declared public lift family while preserving the intended sampling process.
nodes.scope: Enumerating rational lifts in increasing certified height boxes defines a partial search rule until termination is proved or an explicit nonterminating family is retained.

nodes.label: Selected-lift height versus global minimal discriminant
nodes.statement: No uniform theorem bounds the heights of the points selected by an explicit xedni lift algorithm against the global minimal discriminant of the selected rational curve family.
nodes.scope: An arbitrary integral model is not intrinsic: admissible scaling changes its discriminant by a twelfth power. The theorem must normalize to a global minimal model and quantify over selected, not all, rational multiples.

nodes.label: Xedni selected-lift reduction and subgroup correspondence
nodes.statement: The selected rational lifts are not yet proved to reduce to the intended finite-field points with the required prime-subgroup sampling, useful nonzero denominators and bounded cofactor uniformly across the family.
nodes.scope: Good reduction alone does not compose selector output with the finite xedni core or the adaptive trial process.

edges.statement: The claimed contraction bound requires a typed predicate description and entry-evaluation cost certificate.
The claimed contraction bound requires aggregate construction-time and polynomial-space accounting.
The hashed route remains conditional until every end-to-end phase is composed under one parameter family.
The relation-count route still needs its target-distribution and usable-yield hypotheses.
Collected relations must meet the route's rank requirement.
The numeric recursion begins beyond the public host representation, so practical fallback execution neither validates nor refutes the asymptotic bound.
The hashed Boolean tensor route is a representation-specific coordinate-algebraic candidate outside a generic table interface.
Without a fixed complete target population, the prime-field distribution shape cannot be measured without stopping bias.
Without the same immutable relation population, terminal rank and support defects cannot be inferred from early independent rows.
The checked field consequence supplies the theory-side object that must be bound to exact Boolean trail literals.
A combined proof log cannot be checked until each field premise and conclusion has an unambiguous Boolean encoding.
A proof-eligible arity-three solver scaling claim needs replayable composition of its theory lemmas and Boolean proof log.
The missing proof-eligible solver is one concrete solver/interface gate in the end-to-end exponent obligation.
The dual nullspace certificate is the finite object whose growing family would prove closure-degree lower bounds.
A growing dual family is one precise proof route into the broader PKM solving-degree question.
Even resolving degree growth does not settle representation-aware matrix width, memory or sparse work.
General degree-dependent cost facts do not supply the missing PKM-specific width lower bound.
Constant first-fall degree does not certify bounded matrix width or arithmetic work.
The W statistic is the precise second moment whose scaling the native panel must determine.
The proposed filter gain requires a favorable scaling law for bucket concentration.
Bucket concentration must be converted into enumerable useful relations with a non-generic witness and complete costs.
The elliptic-curve proposal inherits Wagner-style list and representation hypotheses in addition to its curve-specific bridge.
Any filter gain must survive complete setup, relation, rank, memory and verification accounting.
A useful representation filter would be one concrete coordinate-algebraic escape candidate.
Termination of one explicit selector is a concrete component of the broad xedni end-to-end gap.
The selected-height/global-minimal-discriminant comparison is a concrete component of the broad xedni gap.
Reduction and subgroup correspondence are concrete components of the broad xedni gap.
The conditional obstruction needs an actual uniformly terminating selected-lift process.
The height obstruction requires an intrinsic bound for selected lifts against global minimal discriminants.
The rational-point bound must compose with the intended finite subgroup, useful denominator and cofactor process.
The finite core is checked under explicit hypotheses but does not prove that selector outputs satisfy them.

research_targets.label: Certify hashed-tensor predicate and aggregate costs
research_targets.objective: Replace opaque predicate admission with a typed canonical family carrying checkable description and per-operation bounds, then compose local allocations into the source construction-time and polynomial-space theorem.
research_targets.acceptance: A versioned certificate schema, fail-closed checker, theorem-to-code matrix and proof that every admitted network meets the source predicate-evaluation, construction and aggregate-space hypotheses; arbitrary closures remain ineligible.
research_targets.next_step: Define the canonical predicate-family cost algebra and check it against every live hashed-tensor predicate before attempting the aggregate recursion proof.

research_targets.label: Fixed-budget write-once yield and rank population
research_targets.objective: Measure the complete target-wise decomposition-count distribution and incremental relation-rank/support law from one immutable natural-target population without adaptive stopping.
research_targets.acceptance: A clean native successor namespace with public fixture derivation, fixed ordered targets and budget, all zero and failed counts, every replayed sparse row, rank after each row, dead columns, components, 2-core and frozen random-base/graph nulls; all source, binary, protocol and output hashes retained.
research_targets.next_step: Resolve fixture provenance by deriving a public successor identity; do not rerun, reclaim or relabel the held historical batch.
research_targets.notes: Blocked on clean fixture custody, not on compute availability.

research_targets.label: Compose arity-three Fp and Boolean proofs
research_targets.objective: Turn the native unit-equation checker into a production proof-eligible external propagator by binding canonical field assignments to Boolean literals and composing every emitted consequence with a pinned Boolean proof log.
research_targets.acceptance: Mutation-tested bidirectional literal/value encoding, CaDiCaL integration, independent replay of every field explanation and Boolean clause, and explicit checked certificate types for each stronger lemma rule before the natural/planted/UNSAT scaling panel is frozen.
research_targets.next_step: Implement and exhaustively test the canonical field-value to selector-literal binding without adding a stronger algebraic lemma class.

research_targets.label: PKM dual lower bounds and matrix-width bridge
research_targets.objective: Implement an independent closure-dual verifier, search for a structured family of growing certificates, and prove what that family implies for the canonical PKM matrix representation's width, memory and work.
research_targets.acceptance: Canonical A_c construction; independently checked A_c*ell=0 and ell_constant=1 certificates on all claimed cells; a proof for growing c(t), or a preserved bounded failure; and a separate theorem or counterexample connecting the result to column support, nonzeros, peak frontier, memory and sparse work.
research_targets.next_step: Build the finite exact verifier and replay it on small measured tower cells before searching the popcount/carry structured ansatz.

research_targets.label: Native Wagner bucket-variance scaling panel
research_targets.objective: Implement and validate the exact W estimator, determine its scaling on the frozen p/M ladder, and separately decide whether any observed concentration yields an enumerable non-generic relation filter.
research_targets.acceptance: Native Rust producer and replay; exact whole-group anchors at the two smallest primes; frozen eight-prime and M ladder; discrete-log-interval positive control; SHA and matched-marginal nulls; jackknife/bias checks; checkpointed admitted execution; and symmetric reporting of small-W and large-W outcomes without upgrading concentration into an attack.
research_targets.next_step: Implement the exact-anchor and estimator-replay path in Rust, then freeze the finite budget before requesting EKS Spot execution.

research_targets.label: Xedni selector, minimal model and reduction bridge
research_targets.objective: Specify one public lift family and explicit selector, then prove termination, selected-height/global-minimal-discriminant control and reduction/subgroup correspondence, or retain the first explicit counterfamily.
research_targets.acceptance: A total selector or explicit nontermination witness; certified global-minimal-model normalization; a uniform selected-point height ratio theorem or unbounded counterfamily; and good-reduction, prime-subgroup, useful-denominator and cofactor correspondence with exact quantifiers.
research_targets.next_step: Define the increasing-certified-height-box selector and one public curve/lift family, then separate the termination proof from the minimal-model height inequality.
